title: Exprimer une exigence, un souhait, une réaction
summary: Choose subjunctive clauses or infinitives for needs, wishes and emotional evaluations.
objectives: Select the subjunctive after requirements, wishes and emotional reactions.
Use an infinitive when there is no separate subordinate subject.
Distinguish evaluative adjectives from assertions of certainty.

sections.title: A requirement is not an assertion
paragraphs: Il faut que + subject + subjunctive names an action as necessary. Il faut + infinitive gives a general requirement without naming a separate subject. Il faut is impersonal: il does not refer to a man or an object.

Avoir besoin que + subjunctive specifies what you need someone or something to do. Avoir besoin de + noun or infinitive instead names the needed thing or your own needed action. A noun is introduced with de, but a finite clause is introduced directly with que, not de que.

examples.french: Il faut que le technicien **vienne** aujourd'hui.
examples.english: The technician needs to come today.
The brakes need to be checked.
examples.note: The infinitive gives a general requirement.

examples.french: J'ai besoin que tu **tiennes** la lampe.
examples.english: I need you to hold the lamp.

examples.note: The person needing and resting is the same.

mistakes.avoid: J'ai besoin de que tu m'aides.
mistakes.why: Use que directly before the finite clause; de belongs before a noun or infinitive.

sections.title: A wish or reaction can concern something real
paragraphs: Vouloir que selects the subjunctive when a separate subject performs the desired action. With the same subject, use vouloir + infinitive: je veux partir. In je veux que tu partes, veux is indicative and partes is subjunctive.

Aimer que and détester que introduce an emotional attitude toward a clause and select the subjunctive. This does not claim the event is doubtful: you can dislike a noise that really occurs every day. With your own activity, aimer/détester + infinitive is the normal compact construction.
points: Je voudrais que is a more courteous wish than je veux que; both select a subjunctive.
Do not treat any occurrence of que as a subjunctive trigger: je constate que asserts an observation and normally takes the indicative.

examples.french: Je veux que vous **preniez** le temps de lire.
examples.english: I want you to take the time to read.
I would like to understand your decision.
examples.note: Same subject, so no que-clause is needed.

examples.french: J'aime que mes voisins **me disent** bonjour.
examples.english: I like my neighbours saying hello to me.
examples.note: A welcome habit, not an uncertain event.

examples.french: Je déteste qu'on **laisse** la porte ouverte.
examples.english: I hate people leaving the door open.

mistakes.why: For a straightforward same-subject wish, use the infinitive; pars is also not subjunctive.

sections.title: The adjective's meaning determines the construction
paragraphs: Impersonal evaluations such as il est important/nécessaire/utile/regrettable/possible que normally select the subjunctive. With a general action, use il est + adjective + de + infinitive. In contrast, il est certain/évident/vrai que normally asserts the clause and takes the indicative when affirmative. 'Il est + adjective' is therefore not one universal mood rule.

examples.french: Il est important que chaque voix **soit** entendue.
examples.english: It is important for every voice to be heard.

examples.french: Il est certain que cette méthode **fonctionne**.
examples.english: It is certain that this method works.
examples.note: An assertion of certainty; fonctionne is indicative here.

examples.french: Il est utile **de garder** une copie.
examples.english: It is useful to keep a copy.
examples.note: No separate subject is expressed after the adjective.

sections.title: Interdire ou laisser le choix
paragraphs: The scope of a negative is what it actually denies. Il ne faut pas que tu viennes normally means you must not come: it prohibits the action, rather than merely making attendance optional. To remove a requirement, say il n'est pas nécessaire que tu viennes or tu n'as pas besoin de venir. Choose the message before choosing the verb form.

Negating an emotional preference does not turn it into an assertion: je n'aime pas que still takes the subjunctive. Keep track of which clause is negative. Je ne veux pas que tu partes rejects your leaving; je veux que tu ne partes pas asks you not to leave. These can lead to the same practical request, but their grammatical negatives sit in different clauses. A negative need such as je n'ai pas besoin que tu viennes still permits the normal subjunctive construction.
points: Do not translate English 'do not have to' mechanically as il ne faut pas que.
A negation is not a universal mood switch: the negative opinions and knowledge statements in the next lesson require their own analysis.

examples.french: Il **ne faut pas que** les visiteurs **touchent** les maquettes.
examples.english: Visitors must not touch the models.

examples.french: Il **n'est pas nécessaire que** les visiteurs **réservent** en semaine.
examples.english: Visitors do not need to book on weekdays.

examples.french: Je **n'aime pas que** tu **répondes** à ma place.
examples.english: I don't like you answering for me.
examples.note: The negative emotional judgement retains the subjunctive.

examples.french: J'ai besoin que vous **ne déplaciez pas** cette table.
examples.english: I need you not to move this table.
examples.note: The need is affirmative; the requested action is negative.

examples.french: Je **n'ai pas besoin que** vous **restiez** après la réunion.
examples.english: I don't need you to stay after the meeting.
examples.note: Staying is unnecessary; the speaker is not issuing a ban.

mistakes.avoid: Il ne faut pas que vous apportiez un ordinateur.
mistakes.prefer: Il n'est pas nécessaire que vous apportiez un ordinateur.
mistakes.why: For the intended message that bringing one is optional, use the second sentence. The first is grammatical but normally prohibits bringing one.

practice.prompt: A laboratory forbids opening a sealed cabinet. Which instruction communicates that ban?
choices: Il ne faut pas que vous ouvriez cette armoire.
Il n'est pas nécessaire que vous ouvriez cette armoire.
answers: Il ne faut pas que vous ouvriez cette armoire.
practice.explanation: Il ne faut pas que normally prohibits; absence of necessity does not prohibit.

practice.prompt: Supply prendre in the present tense with the appropriate mood: Je n'aime pas qu'on ___ des décisions sans consulter l'équipe.
practice.explanation: Negative aimer que remains an emotional evaluation and selects the subjunctive.

practice.prompt: Attendance is optional. Supply être in the present tense: Il n'est pas nécessaire que les stagiaires ___ présents samedi.
practice.explanation: The negative evaluation removes necessity and retains the subjunctive.

practice.prompt: Supply faire in the present tense: Je n'ai pas besoin que tu ___ une copie; j'ai déjà l'original.
practice.explanation: A negative need does not require an indicative; the normal que-clause is subjunctive.

practice.prompt: The speaker needs silence during a recording. Fill the gap with present-subjunctive parler and full ne...pas: J'ai besoin que vous ___ pendant la prise.
practice.explanation: Negate the requested speaking, not the existence of the need.

practice.prompt: What does Tu n'as pas besoin de signer aujourd'hui establish about signing today?
choices: It is not required today; it may still be allowed.
answers: It is not required today; it may still be allowed.
practice.explanation: No need is different from a prohibition.

practice.prompt: Supply venir in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'elle ___ avant huit heures.
practice.explanation: Il faut que requires the subjunctive of venir.

practice.prompt: Complete with avoir: J'ai besoin que vous ___ une pièce d'identité. Present subjunctive only.
practice.explanation: Avoir besoin que selects a subjunctive clause.

practice.prompt: Supply faire in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Je voudrais que tu ___ un essai.
practice.explanation: A courteous wish with a different subject requires fasse + s.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: J'aime que les consignes ___ claires.
practice.explanation: Aimer que selects the subjunctive, even for an actual quality.

practice.prompt: Supply savoir in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Il est nécessaire que nous ___ la vérité.
practice.explanation: Necessity selects the subjunctive.

practice.prompt: Supply prendre in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Je déteste que tu ___ des risques inutiles.
practice.explanation: The emotional evaluation selects prennes.

practice.prompt: Supply only the missing preposition: J'ai besoin ___ dormir.
practice.explanation: Avoir besoin de + infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply only the missing preposition: Il est préférable ___ attendre.
practice.explanation: De elides before attendre.

practice.prompt: Complete with partir for the speaker's own wish: Je veux ___ demain. Infinitive only.
practice.explanation: Same-subject vouloir takes an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply pouvoir in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Il faut que chacun ___ poser une question.
practice.explanation: Chacun is singular; the requirement takes the subjunctive.

practice.prompt: Choose the neutral affirmative assertion: Il est évident qu'elle ___ raison.
practice.explanation: Affirmative il est évident que normally asserts the proposition.

practice.prompt: In Je déteste qu'il soit toujours en retard, is the lateness necessarily uncertain?
choices: No; it may be an established habit.
answers: No; it may be an established habit.
practice.explanation: Emotional evaluation, not probability, selects the mood.

practice.prompt: Supply tenir in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Nous avons besoin qu'ils ___ leurs engagements.
practice.explanation: The requested action is a subjunctive clause.

practice.prompt: Supply revenir in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Elle veut que nous ___ la semaine prochaine.
practice.explanation: Vouloir que selects the subjunctive; nous uses reven-.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present tense, choosing the appropriate mood: Il est regrettable que le jardin ___ fermé.
practice.explanation: Regret evaluates the closure without denying its reality.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present tense for the normal indicative assertion: Il est vrai que nous ___ en retard.
practice.explanation: Il est vrai que presents the clause as true.

production_task.prompt: Write a courteous message to a shared-office group: one need, one preference, one complaint about a real habit and one general recommendation. Use both finite clauses and an infinitive.
production_task.model_answer: J'ai besoin que la salle soit libre à dix heures. Je voudrais que nous commencions à l'heure. Je déteste qu'on interrompe les autres. Il est utile de préparer ses questions à l'avance.
production_task.translation: I need the room to be free at ten. I would like us to start on time. I hate people interrupting others. It is useful to prepare your questions in advance.
rubric: Each selected construction has the appropriate mood or infinitive.
The complaint does not imply that the habit is imaginary.
The tone remains suitable for colleagues.
